cron.title: Scheduled tasks
cron.intro: One small runner exposes independent scheduled tasks with shared authentication.
cron.access_help: Shared endpoint and authentication used by every scheduled task.
cron.query_help: For URL-only hosting schedulers: HTTP Basic authentication, username scheduler, password equal to the cron token. HTTPS is required. GET runs the task; HEAD only checks availability.
cron.rotate_confirm: Rotate the cron token? Existing scheduled calls will stop working until they are updated.

tasks.cleanup_help: Removes unused tags and links, orphaned post and preview images, expired data caches, old rate-limit buckets, expired reset tokens and read notifications.
tasks.cleanup_schedule: Schedule hourly. Internal due checks prevent cleanup from running too often.
tasks.feeds_help: Publishes items from active sources whose interval is due.
tasks.feeds_schedule: Schedule according to the required polling frequency, typically every two minutes.

cron.list_help: Scheduling is controlled by your server or web-cron. These are the recommended intervals and default limits. Run now bypasses the cleanup interval; RSS still respects each source interval. History includes runs recorded after this update.
cron.no_runs: No recorded runs match these filters.
cron.run_failed: The task failed. See its result in the run history.
cron.overview_help: Recommended intervals and default limits. Scheduling is managed by the server or web-cron.
